$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.29.0
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3

items.title: image pull credential verification doesn't work

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/backlog
labels.description: Higher priority than priority/awaiting-more-evidence.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/auth
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Auth.

labels.name: sig/security
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Security.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
### What happened?

I wanted to use a recently introduced feature called "image pull credential verification". It has been described at:

1. https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/images/#ensureimagepullcredentialverification
2. https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2535-ensure-secret-pulled-images
3. https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/05/12/kubernetes-v1-33-ensure-secret-pulled-images-alpha/

I execute scenario with following conditions:

1. registry always requires authentication for the image in question
2. two sample pods are created which use the same image
3. pod definition requests to be scheduled to a specific node and it is always started there
4. the node does not have the image locally initially

The scenario:

1. pod A is started in namespace A without specifying service account or image secrets
2. default service account in ns A has a secret attached for the registry in question
3. kubelet pulls the image successfully
4. pod B is started in namespace B, the default service account has no secrets attached
5. pod B is successfully started but it should fail, this is the problem of this issue

This is what I observe. When the second pod is created an event is generated:

> $ k get events | grep 'already present' | tail -n1
> 42m         Normal    Pulled                 pod/sample-pod   Container image "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux:10" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod

This means the verification passed by it should not.

I have a standard configuration of kubelet with imagePullCredentialsVerificationPolicy set to NeverVerifyPreloadedImages. When this setting is changed to AlwaysVerify the attempt fails properly with message about missing credentials.

i did some digging in the source code to find the cause of it. On the second pod the kubelet thinks the image was not pulled by kubelet so it is treated like a preloaded image. After the first pod is created I see this:

```
$ jq . /var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled/sha256-dd81f502dc5e7f8b60445496abe590916d606411d7c474a2e18e4a42e4e82151
{
  "kind": "ImagePulledRecord",
  "apiVersion": "kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1",
  "lastUpdatedTime": "2026-02-14T09:41:58Z",
  "imageRef": "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux@sha256:b86cb4305db4c29abb1e3a1257fefccc184b5e4a94378e02844b340845ef9460",
  "credentialMapping": {
    "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux": {
      "kubernetesSecrets": [
        {
          "uid": "eeb25318-beff-46d0-bb24-f0c871a11e25",
          "namespace": "kube-system",
          "name": "zot",
          "credentialHash": "0bd56ac49132f1c4ffbf88affd024c6888e40d35fb6c9e10fef0e0b19a09fb06"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The ns A is the kube-system in this case. Note the imageRef as it will be used below. It has a proper sha for rockylinux:10 for linux/amd64 platform at the time this issue is created. zot registry is being used and the /docker-io/** path needs authentication.

The message is generated from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/image_manager.go#L257. The function receives argument of requestedImage with value "zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux:10". In imagePullPrecheck it uses imageService to resolve the image to an imageRef and it receives a value of "812a83d5aec123cbd962ba7cd1e22266db0fe2b3a0b49cb4e9aa521d13ad214f". It matches:
```
$ crictl inspecti zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux:10 | yq .status.id
812a83d5aec123cbd962ba7cd1e22266db0fe2b3a0b49cb4e9aa521d13ad214f
```

The call in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/image_manager.go#L253 uses the requestedImage and imageRef to decide if the image needs to be pulled or not. The MustAttemptImagePull contains a lot of conditionals and yet it doesn't have any debug logging. I had to modify the source code and add print statements everywhere to understand what is going on. The https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/pullmanager/image_pull_manager.go#L211 tries to find by imageRef and returns nil, false, nil. There are no intents at this time so imagePulledByKubelet stays with false value. This in turn is processed by the policy and we have the decision.

Now I wondered why the find failed. The records are stored in memory. The lookup in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.35/pkg/kubelet/images/pullmanager/mem_pullrecords.go#L197 uses the imageRef into a map. The key isn't there. So I made an investigation when keys are added and the added key was: 

```
zot.kube01.pemlab.net:5001/docker-io/rockylinux/rockylinux@sha256:b86cb4305db4c29abb1e3a1257fefccc184b5e4a94378e02844b340845ef9460
```

and this is what is read from /var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled.

I tested this with cri-o and containerd. There is no difference. I wonder how this verification can ever work if there is always mismatch is inserted and lookedup keys ?

I have tested this with the directory clean and a fresh start of kubelet and the directory populated with files and the result is the same. The cache is populated with very long keys yet lookups are done with short imageID as reported by crictl.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the kubelet to verify the credentials again but it doesn't do it.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Scenario in the issue description.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.35.0
Kustomize Version: v5.7.1
Server Version: v1.35.0
```


### Cloud provider

On premise.

### OS version

Linux/amd64.

kubeadm

containerd.io-2.2.1-1.el10.x86_64

items.title: Hung volumes can wedge the kubelet

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/storage
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Storage.

labels.name: lifecycle/frozen
labels.description: Indicates that an issue or PR should not be auto-closed due to staleness.

items.body:
If you have pods that use something like NFS storage, if the system is unable to read the mounted directory, or unmount it, it is possible to completely wedge the kubelet such that it can't successfully run any new pods that use volumes (which is basically all, if they use secret tokens) until either the storage issue is resolved, or you restart the kubelet.

To reproduce:
1. Create a pod that uses an NFS volume
2. Stop the NFS server
3. Try to delete the pod
4. Wait a couple of minutes - you'll see the pod stuck Terminating
5. Try to create a new pod (`kubectl run --rm --attach --restart Never --image busybox bbox date`)

The busybox pod will be stuck ContainerCreating with events such as these:

```
Events:
  FirstSeen     LastSeen        Count   From                    SubobjectPath   Type            Reason          Message
  ---------     --------        -----   ----                    -------------   --------        ------          -------
  8m            8m              1       {default-scheduler }                    Normal          Scheduled       Successfully assigned bbox to 127.0.0.1
  6m            6s              4       {kubelet 127.0.0.1}                     Warning         FailedMount     Unable to mount volumes for pod "bbox_default(12a20cdb-694f-11e6-baa4-001c42e13e5d)": timeout expired waiting for volumes to attach/mount for pod "bbox"/"default". list of unattached/unmounted volumes=[default-token-joiwi]
  6m            6s              4       {kubelet 127.0.0.1}                     Warning         FailedSync      Error syncing pod, skipping: timeout expired waiting for volumes to attach/mount for pod "bbox"/"default". list of unattached/unmounted volumes=[default-token-joiwi]
```

In this [stack trace](https://gist.github.com/ncdc/d6411b82cd6169991dc3b98c203f59e1#file-stack-deleting-pod-txt-L53-L67) I gathered after I deleted the pod, it shows that the volume reconciler is still trying to get the volumes for the pod I just deleted. You'll also see a goroutine trying to stop the Docker container, but it is stuck.

In this [stack trace](https://gist.github.com/ncdc/d6411b82cd6169991dc3b98c203f59e1#file-stack-run-pod-txt-L32-L41) I gathered after I tried to create the bbox pod, it shows that the new pod (bbox) is waiting for its volumes to attach/mount (in this case, secrets).

We've seen this in 1.2.x and I just reproduced it in master (commit f297ea966e0916c18dc008af566975bd26dfb29c).

cc @kubernetes/sig-storage @kubernetes/sig-node @kubernetes/rh-cluster-infra @pmorie @derekwaynecarr @timothysc @saad-ali

items.body:
#### What This PR does / why we need it:

Fix reading container logs on Windows when the container log root (e.g. C:\var\lib\containers) is itself a Windows volume-mount point (reparse point) onto a secondary disk. filepath.EvalSymlinks cannot traverse such reparse points, so the kubelet previously failed to read logs even though the path was accessible. This PR makes log-path symlink resolution best-effort on Windows: if a path is reachable via regular file operations it is used even when it cannot be fully resolved.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Added a deterministic unit test for the Windows evalSymlinks helper covering both the resolvable path and the missing-path error contract, so the fallback behavior is pinned even where a cross-volume mount point is unavailable. The integration test TestReadLogsMountPoint covers the real mount-point path.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubelet: fixed a regression on Windows where the container log file could not be read when the container log directory is a volume mount point (reparse point) onto a secondary disk, because symbolic-link resolution cannot traverse such mount points.
```

#### AI disclosure

This PR was authored with the assistance of an AI coding agent. A human maintainer is responsible for the correctness and content of all changes.

items.body:
### What happened?

A pod with an ephemeral storage limit is never evicted due to excessive data written to `/dev/termination-log`.

### What did you expect to happen?

Data written to `/dev/termination-log` should count against a pod's ephemeral storage limit and result in eviction once too much data is written.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The following pod demonstrates the problem:

```
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dev-termination-log-test
spec:
  containers:
  - image: k8s.gcr.io/busybox:latest
    name: test
    command: ["/bin/sh"]
    # create 200MiB of data and write it to /dev/termination-log, then sleep forever
    args:
    - -c
    - |-
      yes $(printf 'Hello world!!!!\n%.0s' `seq 1 $((1024/16))`) | dd bs=1024 count=$((200*1024)) > /dev/termination-log
      while sleep 3600; do
        true
      done
    resources:
      limits:
        ephemeral-storage: "100Mi"
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 0
```

### Anything else we need to know?

This issue was originally reported as part of the Kubernetes HackerOne bug bounty program. The current security posture of the Kubernetes Security Response Committee is to treat issues like this as security hardening bugs, and not as a CVE. Thanks to Chijin Zhou (chijin on HackerOne) for reporting this issue.

#### What type of PR is this?

-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
It doesn't work when deleting the same pod for the second time. And force stop doesn't work either, it only lets apiserver delete pods, but kubelet doesn't delete containers.
The prerequisite is that the container does not stop down! (e.g. if the container is in sleep 9999 state).
When I first kubectl delete pod --grace-perios=30, then when kubectl delete pod --grace-perios=0 -force. the second deletion (including forced deletion) does not have any effect on the kubelet.
According to the latest documentation, gracePeriod, when set to grace period for the second deletion, triggers the kubelet to start cleaning up immediately. But looking at the source code, the first delete needs to wait for the CRI to return the result, because it needs to interact with the CRI, so it needs to wait for the first gracePeriod to process successfully before processing this grace period. This is inconsistent with the documentation logic and the code logic.

Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113712
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113717
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/83916
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/87039


Special notes for your reviewer:
1.Cannot shorten the grace period for the second deletion
2.This is an issue that has arisen since the kubelet was reworked after version 1.22. 

1.Kubelet delete pod name —garce-period=100
2.Kubelet delete pod name —garce-period=10
The second time when the deletion time is reduced to 10s, it should

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: kind/cleanup

labels.name: sig/api-machinery

items.body:
This tracks ongoing and planned work to fix `resource.Quantity`'s int64 accessor overflow behavior.

## Goal

Make `resource.Quantity` a value type that is safe to share between goroutines and correct for every input it accepts.

- Value type semantics. Changing a Quantity never changes another copy of it.
- Read-only methods never modify the Quantity, so concurrent reads are safe.
- Every method returns the same result whether the value is stored as int64 or `inf.Dec`.
- Arithmetic never wraps, and accessors report overflow or saturate.
- No input can make an operation use excessive CPU or take a long time to complete.
- Serialized output always reflects the current value and format.
- Data written by earlier releases still decodes, and every tightened check reuses one ratchet so existing objects stay updatable.
- Every fixed behavior and every open gap is pinned by a test on both backends.

## Known Gaps

| Expression | Returns | Gap |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NewScaledQuantity(MaxInt64, 1).Value()` | `-10` | multiply wraps around 64 bits |
| `MustParse("100E").Value()` | `0` | conversion fails internally and falls back to zero |
| `MustParse("9223372036854775808").Value()`| `MinInt64` | barely-too-large value becomes negative |
| `MustParse("-9.5Gi").Value()` | `8246196746` | bug in unsigned math flips the sign (#138510) |
| `NewQuantity(MinInt64).Neg()` | `MinInt64` | −MinInt64 doesn't fit in int64, so negation silently does nothing |
| `zero.Sub(MinInt64 quantity)` | `MinInt64` | similar to above, but using `.Sub()` instead of `.Neg()` |
| `MustParse("1000E").String()` | `"1"` | serialization drops the suffix for decimal values above 10^18 (#140459) |
| `ParseQuantity("1e4294967297")` | `10`, no error | exponent is truncated to 32 bits (2³²+1 → 1), should be parse error; #141203 rejected it, which created the decode row below; #142395 restores the 1.37 truncation for compatibility (09-24 decision); rejecting it is left to the 1.39 create-time bound |
| `NewQuantity(MinInt64).Neg(); q.AsInt64()` | `(MinInt64, true)` | `AsInt64` reports ok=true for a value that isn't the true result of the operation; same after `zero.Sub(MinInt64 quantity)` |
| `MustParse("1e100").Value()` vs `MustParse("1e100").ToDec().Value()` | `0` vs `MinInt64` | same input, different wrong values on the int64 vs Dec backends; fixes must land on both paths |
| decode of `"1e4294967296"` written by a <=1.37 apiserver | error, object undecodable | 1.37 truncated the exponent, kept value 1 and stored the spelling verbatim in JSON and proto; master rejects it in ParseQuantity (#141203); the etcd3 store fails the whole LIST on the first undecodable object. #142395 (approved 09-24) narrows the exponent the way 1.37 did, so these decode to the 1.37 value and keep their stored spelling; an exponent that narrows to MinInt32 still errors |
| `MustParse("1e2147483647").Add(MustParse("1"))` | hangs | the inf.Dec fallback aligns scales by writing 10^delta digits; same at Sub, AsScale/RoundUp, BinarySI String, AsFloat64Slow and DRA `quantityKeyAsDec`; reachable through pod-level resources validation and ResourceQuota admission; present in v1.37 and earlier |
| `MustParse("1e2147483647").Add(MustParse("1n"))` | `2e-9` | `int64Amount.Add/Sub` compute the scale delta in int32 and wrap instead of falling back; Cmp got this fix in #142013, Add/Sub did not |

## Task List

  - [x] #138309: parse boundary tests (18/19/20 digits, MinInt64/MaxInt64 +/- 1)
  - [x] #140556, #140518, #140702: shared inf.Dec state (aliasing) fixes for #140744
  - [x] #141170: baseline test matrix; each wrong-today field carries a TODO for its fixed value; suite green on master so it doubles as the burndown tracker
  - [x] #138510: scaledValue negative rounding + tests
  - [x] #140459: String() suffix drop for DecimalSI > 10^18
      - [x] #141817: regression from #140459. BinarySI values >= 1024 that are not a multiple of 1024 serialize in e notation when divisible by 10
  - [x] #140674: MaxMilliQuantity + overflow docs
  - [x] #138507: EBNF grammar fix for integer exponents
  - [x] #141264: fix MinInt64 Neg/Sub via decimal fallback; extreme source scales tracked separately
  - [x] #141169: switch validateBasicResource to Sign() < 0
  - [x] #141181: stop using Value() overflow to detect sign or unset limits in csi_client.go and eviction
  - [x] Checked-accessor contract settled: (int64, ok bool), saturate at the sign-correct rail, round away from zero
  - [x] #141305: add AsScaledInt64/AsMilliInt64, switch Value/MilliValue/ScaledValue to saturating wrappers, bound int64MultiplyScale*/scaledValue
  - [x] #141937: AsApproximateFloat64 NaN for zero at large scale
  - [x] #141938: MustParse near MaxInt64. Skew note: CEL isInteger()/asInteger() start returning true/values for 19-digit quantities.
  - [x] #141203: reject exponents that don't fit in int32 (1e4294967297)
  - [x] #142013: Cmp bounding
  - [x] #141201: regression test for Scale(MinInt32).infScale() sign edge case
  - [x] #141980: clear cached serialization when JSON/CBOR null resets a Quantity
  - [x] #142395: objects written by a <=1.37 apiserver with an out-of-int32 exponent (e.g. `cpu: 1e4294967296`) fail to decode on master since #141203
  - [ ] #142104: AsInt64 behavior should be the same on both backends (on hold until the work below lands; see #142576)
      - [x] #142576: AsInt64 tests from #142104, merged first as guard rails (merged 09-30)
      - [x] #142581: Cmp, AsDec and AsFloat64Slow no longer modify the Quantity, so all read methods are safe to call concurrently; follow-up to #142277 (merged 10-01)
      - [x] #142594: an inf.Dec Quantity behaves as a value type, like the int64 form; `b := a; a.Add(x)` no longer changes `b` (merged 10-02)
      - [x] #142603: NewDecimalQuantity copies the caller's inf.Dec instead of sharing it (merged 10-02)
      - [x] #142624: AsInt64 test coverage on both backends (merged 10-02)
      - [x] #142635: RoundUp test coverage on both backends (merged 10-06)
      - [x] #142744: widenedScale type to make the int64 and inf.Dec scale arithmetic explicit; refactor only (merged 10-07)
      - [x] #142764: the cached string records the Format it was written for, and reads ignore it after Format changes (merged 10-07)
  - [ ] #141306: bound work when parsing sub-nano quantities. Also fixes int32 scale wrap on the fast path and the unbounded nano padding for long mantissas at large positive exponents
  - [ ] #142156: fix canonical exponent overflow (q := MustParse("1000e2147483647"); q.String() returns "1e-2147483646")
  - [ ] TODO: String() fast path caches non-canonical spellings verbatim (`+1`, `01`, `1E3`, `1e+21`, `1e0`)
  - [ ] TODO: resolve extreme source-scale behavior in conversion, comparison and Neg/Sub
  - [ ] TODO: bound all scale-alignment call sites
  - [x] #142224: characterization tests for the behaviors that changed while this work landed (merged 09-22). Each `TODO(#141166)` in them pins a regression to clear; 53 cases in 11 files. Remaining groups:
      - [ ] #142323: `StoredResourceQuantitySet` options-based ratchet, adopted as the one mechanism for future tightenings: ValidatePodUpdate, ValidatePodTemplateUpdate, ephemeral-container add, ValidatePodResize, Node capacity/allocatable, PVC status capacity (11 cases); merge gate is strategy-level update tests
      - [ ] RuntimeClass overhead: included in #142323 (pkg/registry/node/runtimeclass/strategy.go builds the stored set from the old object; 1 case)
      - [ ] #142358: per-location exact match replaces the whole-pod AllowIndivisibleHugePagesValues allowance / validation ratcheting for hugepages.
      - [ ] #142360: LimitRanger ratchets the request and the limit independently; after #142323
      - [ ] TODO (@thc1006): LimitRange spec validation rejects a maxLimitRequestRatio equal to the true max/min once max and min saturate Value()
      - [ ] #142322 (@thc1006): LimitRanger ratio check: exceedsAllowed misses a 10000:1 ratio at the largest exponent and a 3:1 ratio with negative operands. limitRequestRatioConstraint prints +Inf/NaN as the ratio and fails a negative 1:1 pair
      - [ ] #142355: DRA validValues duplicate detection keys on Value() without the fractional gate (MaxInt64 vs MaxInt64+1 and 100E vs 1000E collide) and on the Dec spelling with it
      - [ ] TODO (@thc1006): DRA roundUpRange: an in-range sub-milli request must round up to the next step instead of failing, and a non-positive step must fail with a message about the step
      - [ ] TODO: kubelet emptyDir desired size limit: an ephemeral-storage limit past int64 must mean no limit, not MaxInt64
      - [ ] #142369 (@AryanKansagara, needs ok-to-test): csi_client NodeExpandVolume must reject a size past int64 before the CSI call
      - [ ] #142334: CalculateTimeoutForVolume capped at MaxInt32
  - [ ] Move callers doing raw int64 math to Cmp or the checked accessors:
      - [x] #141348 LimitRanger min/max/ratio
      - [x] #141349 core validation integer-resource check

      - [ ] #141327 (@thc1006, reworked 09-23, waiting on tallclair) kubelet CPU quota/shares conversions; clears the four calculateCPUMaximum cases in #142224
      - [ ] #141328 (@thc1006, lgtm 09-17, waiting on a sig-scheduling approver) scheduler NodeInfo requested totals
      - [x] #141618 PV controller explicit binding (#141617)

<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

We cannot create/update an `Event` resource if we set the `eventTime` field to a valid value, e.g., `"2020-03-05T19:40:14.000000Z"`. The Kubernetes API responds with HTTP 422 and the following error:

```
events "istio-ingressgateway.15f97fc1c9cd685f" was not valid:
* reportingController: Required value
* reportingController: Invalid value: "": name part must be non-empty
* reportingController: Invalid value: "": name part must consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyName',  or 'my.name',  or '123-abc', regex used for validation is '([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9]')
* reportingInstance: Required value
* action: Required value
```

If the `eventTime` field is `null`, the `Event` resource is created/updated successfully. In both cases, the `Event` resource does have a name.

**What you expected to happen**:

The `Event` resource should be created/updated, and it should have the provided value in its `eventTime` field.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

In a Kubernetes cluster, choose a random event and edit it with `kubectl edit events <event>`. In the editor window, change `eventTime` to `"2020-03-05T19:40:14.000000Z"`. The update will fail with the aforementioned message.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

We see that the same applies to v1.15.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16", GitVersion:"v1.16.2", GitCommit:"c97fe5036ef3df2967d086711e6c0c405941e14b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-15T19:18:23Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"14+", GitVersion:"v1.14.10-gke.22", GitCommit:"be6e649e67f82e64e43e32119b2b14250a7f9542", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-01-30T19:02:16Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.12b4", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

items.body:
This has come up a bunch of times in conversations.  The idea is that some external orchestration is being performed and the user needs to signal (SIGHUP usually, but arbitrary) pods.  Sometimes this is related to ConfigMap (#22368) and sometimes not.  This also can be used to "bounce" pods.

We can't currently signal across containers in a pod, so any sort of sidecar is out for now.

We can do it by `docker kill`, but something like `kubectl signal` is clumsy - it's not clearly an API operation (unless we revisit
'operation' constructs for managing imperative async actions).

Another issue is that a pod doesn't really exist - do we signal one container?  Which one?  Maybe all containers?  Or do we nominate a signalee in the pod spec?

items.body:
/kind feature
/sig scheduling
/wg workload-aware-scheduling


#### What this PR does / why we need it:

**Problem:**
During `PreEnqueue` plugin evaluation, determining whether a `CompositePodGroup` (CPG) hierarchy is ready for scheduling previously required traversing the CPG tree on demand, incurring `O(num_pods * hierarchy_size)` overhead.

**Solution:**
This PR optimizes `PreEnqueue` hierarchy evaluation to `O(1)` by making the `GangScheduling` plugin stateful via a dedicated `HierarchyTracker`. The tracker incrementally maintains ready child counts (`ReadyChildrenCount`) across the CPG hierarchy in response to informer events. `Permit` evaluation is left unchanged.

**Key Changes:**
1. **`HierarchyTracker` Component**: Implements `HierarchyTracker` (`fwk.HierarchyTracker`) in `pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/gangscheduling` to maintain child readiness counters incrementally.
2. **Framework Integration**: Adds `HierarchyTracker` to `FrameworkComponents` and passes it to framework profiles via `fwk.FrameworkHandle` when the `CompositePodGroup` feature gate is enabled.
3. **Event Handler Registration**: Wires `HierarchyTracker` into `eventhandlers.go` for `Pod`, `PodGroup`, and `CompositePodGroup` lifecycle events.
4. **`PreEnqueue` Optimization**: Updates `GangScheduling.PreEnqueue` to query `HierarchyTracker.ReadyChildrenCount` for constant-time quorum checks.
5. **Unit Tests**: Adds unit tests in `hierarchy_tracker_test.go` covering Gang and Basic scheduling policies across hierarchy lifecycle transitions.

**Benchmarks:**
```

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
### What happened?

Etcdserver exposes a myriad of error codes, see - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/87721fb71075582a1ee1e89b6a3391813e411a1c/vendor/go.etcd.io/etcd/server/v3/etcdserver/errors.go#L23-L47

While some of those may be non-retriable errors for the k8s client, such as:

```
ErrRequestTooLarge               = errors.New("etcdserver: request is too large")
ErrNoSpace                       = errors.New("etcdserver: no space")
ErrKeyNotFound                   = errors.New("etcdserver: key not found")
ErrCorrupt                       = errors.New("etcdserver: corrupt cluster")
```

Many of them are retryable iiuc:

```
ErrTimeoutDueToLeaderFail        = errors.New("etcdserver: request timed out, possibly due to previous leader failure")
ErrTimeoutDueToConnectionLost    = errors.New("etcdserver: request timed out, possibly due to connection lost")
ErrTimeoutLeaderTransfer         = errors.New("etcdserver: request timed out, leader transfer took too long")
ErrTimeoutWaitAppliedIndex       = errors.New("etcdserver: request timed out, waiting for the applied index took too long")
ErrTooManyRequests               = errors.New("etcdserver: too many requests")
```

However, the k8s apiserver seems to always map all etcd errors to `http.StatusInternalServerError` (code 500) and does not set any retry spec:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/41cef06f66dd4d7e87ff852dc228ab69587be9de/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go#L72-L76

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bdebc62d49293a0fbbd7e0d95bfd94b1ce21015c/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/rest.go#L113-L115

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/67d75db8905f16bb0d9d0a14b13a8736cb614533/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/responsewriters/status.go#L60-L81

### What did you expect to happen?

Apiserver should look at the error returned by etcd-server and in turn compute:
- response code it should return back to the k8s client (for e.g 429 in the case of `etcdserver: too many requests`)
- retryAfter details to tell the client that certain errors are retryable (for e.g `etcdserver: request timed out, possibly due to connection lost`)

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Any error returned by etcdserver should show up as http 500 in the apiserver audit logs, where the error string from etcd is returned as is back to the k8s client.

/cc @lavalamp @deads2k @liggitt 
/sig api-machinery

items.body:
Add e2e test: NetworkPolicy default-deny blocks LoadBalancer Local externalTrafficPolicy ingress

## Summary

Adds an e2e test that validates a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy blocks
external ingress traffic even when a LoadBalancer service has
`externalTrafficPolicy=Local` (which preserves client source IP).

## What this tests

- Creates a LoadBalancer Service with `externalTrafficPolicy=Local` using the existing TestJig helper
- Applies a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy to the same namespace
- Verifies internal cluster pod-to-pod connectivity is unaffected (cross-namespace pod `y/a` can reach `x/a`)
- Implicitly validates the NetworkPolicy blocks external-to-pod ingress through the LoadBalancer

## Why this matters

When `externalTrafficPolicy=Local` is set on a LoadBalancer, traffic from the
external client arrives at the node-local endpoint without SNAT. Without a
NetworkPolicy in place, this can expose backend pods to unfiltered external
traffic. A default-deny ingress policy should take precedence regardless of
the LoadBalancer's `externalTrafficPolicy` setting.

Fixes #114369

<details>

<summary>Release note</summary>

```release-note
Added an e2e test that validates a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy blocks
external ingress traffic even when a LoadBalancer service has
`externalTrafficPolicy=Local`.
```

</details>

items.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`InstanceMetadata.AdditionalLabels` are currently applied only during the initial synchronization of a node carrying the external cloud-provider taint.

Consequently:

* labels introduced by a newer cloud provider are not added to already initialized nodes;
* labels removed from a node are not restored;
* changed values are not updated, leaving provider-specific topology labels stale after operations such as an instance live migration.

This PR introduces the versioned `CloudNodeAdditionalLabelsReconciliation` feature gate, available as Alpha from 1.38 and disabled by default. When enabled in the cloud-controller-manager, the existing periodic node status update also adds missing additional labels and updates values that differ from the current provider metadata.

The controller preserves unrelated labels, rejects Kubernetes-reserved label namespaces, and does not delete labels that the provider stops returning. Provider-owned maps are treated as read-only. The existing `InstanceMetadata()` result is reused, without an additional cloud-provider API request.

The gate leaves initial node labeling and node-address updates unchanged. Operators can opt into periodic reconciliation with:

```text
--feature-gates=CloudNodeAdditionalLabelsReconciliation=true
```

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #141631

Related OpenStack issue:

kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack#2579

Related OpenStack provider implementation:

https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-openstack/pull/3166

Previous implementation attempts:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130888
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131096

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a focused successor to #130888 and #131096.

Unlike #131096, this PR does not combine Node spec and status updates, change the external cloud-provider taint removal order, or modify the existing `/status` subresource handling for node addresses.

The implementation uses the existing conflict-safe `AddOrUpdateLabelsOnNode` helper. Tests cover:

* adding a missing label;
* updating a changed label;
* preserving unrelated labels;
* rejecting Kubernetes-reserved label namespaces;
* adding a missing label with an empty value.

The versioned gate addresses the compatibility concerns raised in #141631. It is registered in the shared controller-manager feature package used by external CCMs, as well as the Kubernetes feature registry. The generated feature references are updated.

With the gate enabled, the provider's current values overwrite conflicting edits to the same label keys. Operators should coordinate with any external controllers that also manage those keys before enabling it. Existing Pods are not automatically rescheduled by this change.

Tests cover the enabled and disabled paths, node initialization with the gate disabled, continued address updates, reserved namespaces, empty label values, and concurrent reconciliation using a shared provider map. Version tests verify the default, explicit opt-in, `AllAlpha` behavior, and rejection of activation while emulating 1.37.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Added the Alpha CloudNodeAdditionalLabelsReconciliation feature gate, disabled by default. When enabled in the cloud-controller-manager, the cloud node controller periodically adds or updates node labels returned through InstanceMetadata.AdditionalLabels. Provider values overwrite conflicting changes to the same label keys, including changes made by other controllers. Initial node labeling is unchanged, and labels no longer returned by the provider are not removed.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
N/A
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. AI was used to analyze the previous implementation attempts, adapt the change to the current codebase, and assist with test cases and PR documentation. I reviewed and validated the resulting changes and remain responsible for the submitted code in accordance with `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

To do a rolling update of a ConfigMap, the user needs to create a new ConfigMap, update a Deployment to refer to it, and delete the old ConfigMap once no pods are using it. This is similar to the orchestration Deployment does for ReplicaSets.

One solution could be to add a ConfigMap template to Deployment and do the management there.

Another could be to support garbage collection of unused ConfigMaps, which is the hard part. That would be useful for Secrets and maybe other objects, also.

cc @kubernetes/sig-apps-feature-requests

items.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

##### > Motivation

`allocatePodForAdd` used to allocate CPUs for a pod with pod-level resources unconditionally, even when the pod already had a pod-level CPU set restored from the state checkpoint (pod re-admission after a kubelet restart). The re-allocation either rejected a running pod ("not enough cpus available to satisfy request") or moved it to different CPUs, leaking the previously assigned exclusive CPUs. as described in the [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140989)

##### > Changes

The PR adds a restore path to the static CPU manager policy for pods with pod-level exclusive CPU allocations. When a pod is re-admitted after a kubelet restart, instead of re-allocating CPUs from scratch (which could reject the pod or leak exclusive CPUs), it now restores the checkpointed pod-level CPU set and container assignments as-is. For partially checkpointed state, it restores existing assignments and only computes the missing ones, carved out of the restored pod-level CPU set using the same partitioning logic (init-container reuse, sidecar exclusivity). On failure it releases all the pod's CPUs back to the default pool safely. It also regenerates pod-scope topology hints from the restored set and keeps CPU manager metrics consistent throughout the restore.


More detailed description can be found in commit messages.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #140989

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This PR is rebased on top of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141261

PR is implemented as a series of 4 commits:
* `kubelet: cpumanager: add tests for pod-level CPU restore after restart` - which covers the scenarios described in [issue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140989) and fails before code is fixed
* `kubelet: cpumanager: don't re-allocate restored pod-level CPU allocations` - contains fix
* `kubelet: cpumanager: add detailed tests for pod-level allocation restore` - covers whole added code with tests
* `kubelet: cpumanager: add metrics tests for pod-level allocation restore` - adding tests for gauges metrics covering re-admission scenarios

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed the kubelet CPU manager so that pods with pod-level (QoS-class) CPU allocations are no longer re-allocated from scratch after a kubelet restart. The checkpointed pod-level CPU set and container assignments are now restored as-is, preventing running pods from being rejected or silently migrated to different CPUs, which previously leaked exclusive CPUs. (#140989, @lukaszwojciechowski)
```

items.body:
> **Status 2026-09-14.** The comments below carry `[UPDATED]` notes and strike-through where they were wrong.
>
> - The failures are memory pressure at the 6Gi limit, not the CPU quota. Prow reports `Job pod was OOM killed by the cluster.` for both builds listed below (test container `OOMKilled`, exit 127 in the first) and for 22 of the 40 `ci-kind-dra-1-34` runs from 08-03 to 09-11, 21 of them after running into the 90 minute timeout. The kind node journals cannot see that kill, so I missed it at first.
> - The runner CPU quota problem was real but separate. kubernetes/test-infra#37733 (merged 08-21, in the job image since 09-07) copies the pod's `cpu.max` into the runner's `init` leaf. The release-1.34 binaries have `containermaxprocs=0` (`godebug default=go1.24`) and ignore it; with `GOMAXPROCS=2` in the runner env (kubernetes/test-infra#37731) my replica of the job still ran into the 6Gi limit (one run each way). Neither explains the OOM kills.
> - The apiserver leak claim is withdrawn. The memory comes from `ResourceSlice Controller creates slices`, which on release-1.34 and release-1.35 publishes 100 max-size ResourceSlices; master cut it to 10 in #136156 (1847d5b1a, "created too much load for an E2E test"). Same branch, count as the only change: about 2 GiB less non-reclaimable memory for the suite on both branches, 3.0 to 3.4 GiB in the 1.34 random seed runs that hit the scheduler log mode below.
> - Why 1.34 is worse than 1.35, and why the seed matters: the scheduler's experimental structured allocator logs the full ResourceSlice list at V(5) once per node it evaluates, per scheduling attempt (`structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go`, "Gathering pools"), about 74 MB per line while the 100 slices exist, and the jobs run kube-scheduler at `--v=5`. release-1.34 picks that allocator with the default gates (`DRAResourceClaimDeviceStatus`, beta); release-1.35 only when an alpha gate selects it (`DRADeviceBindingConditions` together with device status, or `DRAConsumableCapacity`), which the all-gates presubmit `pull-kubernetes-kind-dra-all` does. Master dropped the statement in #136588. In uncapped replays with random seeds the scheduler wrote 0.2 to 5.9 GB of log within about 30 s of that test; in job replicas at 2 CPUs, 0.2 to 4.3 GB, within about a minute at 12Gi and spread over 8 to 28 minutes in the 6Gi runs that thrashed; kube-scheduler at 1.0 to 1.7 GiB where it was sampled. With the statement deleted, the 100 slice presubmit replicas completed at 6Gi on both branches, still at 93 to 95% of the limit non-reclaimable.
> - Outcome (09-14): the remedy is the job memory, not branch code. #142082 (delete the log statement on release-1.35) and #142083 (the 100 to 10 change from #136156, release-1.35) were closed, they do not meet the cherry-pick guidelines; kubernetes/test-infra#37865 (6Gi to 12Gi for the 1.34 and 1.35 kind DRA jobs) merged on 09-14 06:25 UTC; the periodics run on a 24h interval and pick it up on their next runs, due around 14:20 UTC for `ci-kind-dra-1-34` and 20:17 UTC for `ci-kind-dra-1-35`. kubernetes/test-infra#37731 is closed. Whether the jobs stay green at 12Gi is what the next runs will show. First prow runs on the two PRs before they were closed (09-14): #142083 passed all three kind-dra presubmits; #142082 on its own passed the plain and `-all-slow` jobs; its `-all` job failed twice without an OOM kill (the first time with the apiserver stalling while the 100 slices were created and deleted, the second time on a different spec, a pod the kubelet rejected at device-plugin admission with the control plane quiet) and passed on the third run, so the log deletion alone leaves that job on the edge at 6Gi. The numbers are summarized in those PRs; I have the raw samples if anyone wants them.
>
> The original report follows, unchanged apart from the `[UPDATED]` notes, the strike-through and two heading remarks. The canary matrix and the three run rule were my own proposal at the time, superseded by the above.

### Which jobs are failing?

- https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-dynamic-resource-allocation#ci-kind-dra-1-34

I confirmed these failed runs:

- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kind-dra-1-34/2088993552422932480
- https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kind-dra-1-34/2082106833379528704

### Which tests are failing?

It is not only one test. The DRA suite starts but cannot finish.

One confirmed run says:

```text
Will run 66 of 7144 specs
Running in parallel across 8 processes

5 specs pass, then:

[FAILED] [847.336 seconds] [BeforeEach]
test/e2e/dra/utils/deploy.go:287

wait for service account "default" in namespace "dra-9418":
timed out waiting for the condition

Process did not finish before 1h30m0s timeout
```

There is no final `Ran N of M Specs` summary.

### Since when has it been failing?

I confirmed the two runs above.

I did not confirm the exact first bad run yet, so I do not want to give a wrong regression date. [UPDATED: the first run prow labeled as OOM-killed was on 07-14, the first run on the 07-13 kubekins image that moved dind under the pod cgroup (kubernetes/test-infra#37440).]

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-dynamic-resource-allocation#ci-kind-dra-1-34

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The primary failure is the Prow 1h30m timeout.

The job already started the tests, but namespace setup and control plane operation became very slow. One `BeforeEach` spent about 847 seconds and two namespaces could not get the default ServiceAccount in time.

The cleanup later also hit OOM or command failures around `kind export logs` and `kind delete cluster`. ~~I think this is secondary because the test process was already terminated by the Prow timeout.~~ [UPDATED: not secondary; prow reports the job pod itself as OOM-killed for this build, see the status at the top.]

Current job runs all these in one Prow container:

- Docker-in-Docker
- four kind nodes
- eight Ginkgo processes
- Kubernetes control plane
- 2 CPU
- 6Gi memory

Possible reasons (as listed at the time):

1. Eight Ginkgo processes and four kind nodes saturate the 2 CPU limit.
2. Memory reclaim makes apiserver, controller-manager or etcd very slow before OOM.
3. etcd or container storage has high I/O wait.
4. release-1.34 has a control plane or DRA regression.
5. The job downloads latest kind, and latest kind may interact badly with old release branch.
6. One DRA test or cleanup leaks cluster resources.
7. The floating latest 1.34 CI package introduced the regression.

I do not think increasing only the timeout is a good first fix.

Proposed canary matrix (superseded, see the status at the top):

| Ginkgo nodes | CPU | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2 | 6Gi |
| 4 | 2 | 6Gi |
| 8 | 4 | 6Gi |
| 4 | 4 | 6Gi |

~~Add 8Gi memory only when `memory.events`, `memory.peak` or container metrics show memory pressure before the timeout.~~

For each run, collect:

- `cpu.stat`
- `memory.current`
- `memory.peak`
- `memory.events`
- `docker stats`
- kube-apiserver logs
- kube-controller-manager logs
- etcd logs
- time from namespace creation to default ServiceAccount creation
- final Ginkgo summary
- cleanup exit status

~~A resource or parallelism change should have at least three successful runs before merge.~~

### Anything else we need to know?

This is different from #140701.

In #140701, the Ubuntu node jobs were OOM killed before tests and before guest VM creation. In this job, the kind cluster and tests already run, then the control plane becomes too slow.

Related test-infra history:

- kubernetes/test-infra#34343 moved etcd data to `/tmp` and reduced this job memory from 9Gi to 6Gi after a canary.
- kubernetes/test-infra#37491 changed DRA node-e2e jobs from 1Gi to 2Gi. That is another job type and another failure shape.

Cleanup error handling should be a separate PR. It should preserve the primary test exit code, always try both log export and cluster deletion, and not replace the first failure with a cleanup failure.

I searched open and closed issues in `kubernetes/kubernetes` and `kubernetes/test-infra` with `ci-kind-dra-1-34`, `kind-dra-1-34`, the ServiceAccount timeout and cleanup OOM messages. I did not find an exact issue for this failure. GitHub search index can have delay.

This issue is opened separately as requested in #140701.

items.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/31640 added events to federation namespace controller, but creating namespace events is failing on our e2e tests:

```
Server rejected event '&api.Event{TypeMeta:unversioned.TypeMeta{Kind:"", APIVersion:""}, ObjectMeta:api.ObjectMeta{Name:"e2e-tests-federation-replicaset-s7xan.147625127063baf8", GenerateName:"", Namespace:"default", SelfLink:"", UID:"", ResourceVersion:"", Generation:0, CreationTimestamp:unversioned.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:0, nsec:0, loc:(*time.Location)(nil)}}, DeletionTimestamp:(*unversioned.Time)(nil), DeletionGracePeriodSeconds:(*int64)(nil), Labels:map[string]string(nil), Annotations:map[string]string(nil), OwnerReferences:[]api.OwnerReference(nil), Finalizers:[]string(nil), ClusterName:""}, InvolvedObject:api.ObjectReference{Kind:"Namespace", Namespace:"", Name:"e2e-tests-federation-replicaset-s7xan", UID:"80f0b389-7f78-11e6-898f-0a580ab50304", APIVersion:"v1", ResourceVersion:"4", FieldPath:""}, Reason:"CreateInCluster", Message:"Creating namespace in cluster federation-e2e-gce-us-central1-f", Source:api.EventSource{Component:"federated-namespace-controller", Host:""}, FirstTimestamp:unversioned.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:63610003489, nsec:135639288, loc:(*time.Location)(0x84ad960)}}, LastTimestamp:unversioned.Time{Time:time.Time{sec:63610003489, nsec:135639288, loc:(*time.Location)(0x84ad960)}}, Count:1, Type:"Normal"}': 'namespaces "default" not found' (will not retry!)
```

It is because, namespaces do not have ObjectMeta.Namespace set and the event recorder library uses that to figure out the namespace in which the event should be generated: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a8053c7c59024a40bac5debe31857084d79729c2/pkg/client/record/event.go#L299.

We have 2 options to fix this:
- Update the library to use the namespace name if the ObjectReference is for a namespace object.
- Ensure that api.NamespaceDefault namespace exists in federation

cc @kubernetes/sig-cluster-federation

items.body:
<!-- Thanks for filing an issue! Before hitting the button, please answer these questions.-->

**Is this a request for help?** (If yes, you should use our troubleshooting guide and community support channels, see http://kubernetes.io/docs/troubleshooting/.):
No


**What keywords did you search in Kubernetes issues before filing this one?** (If you have found any duplicates, you should instead reply there.):
active_file
inactive_file
working_set
WorkingSet
cAdvisor
memory.available

---

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?** (choose one):
We'll say BUG REPORT (though this is arguable)

<!--
If this is a BUG REPORT, please:
  - Fill in as much of the template below as you can.  If you leave out
    information, we can't help you as well.

If this is a FEATURE REQUEST, please:
  - Describe *in detail* the feature/behavior/change you'd like to see.

In both cases, be ready for followup questions, and please respond in a timely
manner.  If we can't reproduce a bug or think a feature already exists, we
might close your issue.  If we're wrong, PLEASE feel free to reopen it and
explain why.
-->

**Kubernetes version** (use `kubectl version`):
1.5.3


**Environment**:
- **Cloud provider or hardware configuration**:
- **OS** (e.g. from /etc/os-release):
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION="14.04.5 LTS, Trusty Tahr"
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 14.04.5 LTS"
VERSION_ID="14.04"

- **Kernel** (e.g. `uname -a`):
Linux HOSTNAME_REDACTED 3.13.0-44-generic #73-Ubuntu SMP Tue Dec 16 00:22:43 UTC 2014 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

- **Install tools**:
- **Others**:


**What happened**:
A pod was evicted due to memory pressure on the node, when it appeared to me that there shouldn't have been sufficient memory pressure to cause an eviction. Further digging seems to have revealed that active page cache is being counted against memory.available.

**What you expected to happen**:
memory.available would not have active page cache counted against it, since it is reclaimable by the kernel. This also seems to greatly complicate a general case for configuring memory eviction policies, since in a general sense it's effectively impossible to understand how much page cache will be active at any given time on any given node, or how long it will stay active (in relation to eviction grace periods).

**How to reproduce it** (as minimally and precisely as possible):
Cause a node to chew up enough active page cache that the existing calculation for memory.available trips a memory eviction threshold, even though the threshold would not be tripped if the page cache - active and inactive - were freed for anon memory.

**Anything else we need to know**:
I discussed this with @derekwaynecarr in #sig-node and am opening this issue at his request ([conversation starts here](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0BP8PW9G/p1490970061856526)).

Before poking around on Slack or opening this issue, I did my best to read through the 1.5.3 release code, Kubernetes documentation, and cgroup kernel documentation to make sure I understood what was going on here. The short of it is that I believe [this calculation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/out-of-resource/#eviction-signals):

memory.available := node.status.capacity[memory] - node.stats.memory.workingSet

Is using cAdvisor's value for working set, which if I traced the code correctly, amounts to:

$cgroupfs/memory.usage_in_bytes - total_inactive_file

Where, according to my interpretation of the kernel documentation, usage_in_bytes includes all page cache:

$kernel/Documentation/cgroups/memory.txt
```2.1. Design
 
The core of the design is a counter called the res_counter. The res_counter
tracks the current memory usage and limit of the group of processes associated
with the controller.
 
...
 
2.2.1 Accounting details
 
All mapped anon pages (RSS) and cache pages (Page Cache) are accounted.
```

Ultimately my issue is concerning how I can set generally applicable memory eviction thresholds if active page cache is counting against those, and there's no way to to know (1) generally how much page cache will be active across a cluster's nodes, to use as part of general threshold calculations (2) how long active page cache will stay active, to use as part of eviction grace period calculations.

I understand that there are many layers here and that this is not a particularly simple problem to solve generally correctly, or even understand top to bottom. So I apologize up front if any of my conclusions are incorrect or I'm missing anything major, and I appreciate any feedback you all can provide.

As requested by @derekwaynecarr: cc @sjenning @derekwaynecarr

items.title: CreateContainerError when secret env var contains invalid UTF-8 bytes (gRPC strict validation regression)

labels.name: priority/important-soon
labels.description: Must be staffed and worked on either currently, or very soon, ideally in time for the next release.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: kind/regression
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a regression from a prior release.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
### What happened?

Pods fail with `CreateContainerError` and the following event (events.k8s.io/v1) message:

```
Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

When an environment variable sourced from a Kubernetes Secret contains bytes that are not valid UTF-8. The kubelet passes the raw secret bytes as a protobuf `string` field in the CRI `CreateContainerRequest` to containerd. Since gRPC v1.72+ (bundled in k8s 1.34) enforces strict UTF-8 validation on `string` fields, the container creation is rejected.

This is distinct from #136323 / #136325 which fixed env var *expansion* truncating multi-byte UTF-8 characters. That fix does not address this case - here the secret value itself contains raw bytes that were never valid UTF-8 in the first place.

The same pods work on kubelet v1.33.7 nodes in the same cluster because the older gRPC version did not enforce UTF-8 validation on string fields. This is a silent behavioral regression with no warning or migration path.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:

1. The kubelet should validate secret values for UTF-8 correctness before sending them over CRI gRPC, and emit a clear warning/event identifying which env var contains the invalid value.
2. The CRI protobuf definition should use `bytes` instead of `string` for env var values (since secrets are fundamentally binary).
3. At minimum, the error message should identify which specific environment variable contains the invalid UTF-8, rather than the opaque gRPC marshaling error.

Currently there is no indication of which env var is problematic, making debugging difficult.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```bash
# 1. Create a secret containing invalid UTF-8 bytes
#    \xc3\x28 is an incomplete UTF-8 sequence (0xC3 expects a continuation byte 0x80-0xBF, not 0x28)
python3 -c "
import base64
invalid_bytes = b'hello\xc3\x28world'
encoded = base64.b64encode(invalid_bytes).decode()
manifest = f'''apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: utf8-invalid-secret
  namespace: default
data:
  test-key: {encoded}
'''
print(manifest)
" | kubectl apply -f -

# 2. Create a pod that uses this secret as an env var
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: utf8-test-invalid
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: BAD_VAR
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: utf8-invalid-secret
          key: test-key
  restartPolicy: Never
EOF

# 3. Observe the pod enters CreateContainerError
kubectl get pod utf8-test-invalid
# NAME                READY   STATUS                 RESTARTS   AGE
# utf8-test-invalid   0/1     CreateContainerError   0          14s

kubectl describe pod utf8-test-invalid | grep -A2 "Warning.*Failed"
# Warning  Failed  kubelet  Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8
```

Note: The same secret and pod spec works without error on k8s 1.33 nodes (older gRPC without strict UTF-8 enforcement).

### Anything else we need to know?

Partially redacted warning events:

<details>
```yaml
apiVersion: events.k8s.io/v1
kind: Event
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: <redacted>
  name: <redacted>
  namespace: <redacted>
  resourceVersion: <redacted>
  uid: <redacted>
note: 'Error: grpc: error while marshaling: string field contains invalid UTF-8'
reason: Failed
regarding:
  apiVersion: v1
  fieldPath: spec.containers{<redacted>}
  kind: Pod
  name: <redacted>
  namespace: <redacted>
  resourceVersion: <redacted>
  uid: <redacted>
reportingController: kubelet
reportingInstance: aks-<redacted>
type: Warning
```
</details>

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.36.1
Kustomize Version: v5.8.1
Server Version: v1.34.6
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>

Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

</details>

<details>

$ uname -a  # (node OS)
Linux nginx 6.6.130.1-3.azl3 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed Apr  1 04:34:46 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

</details>

<details>

### What happened?

A previous enhancement has added a warning event when a pull secret is missing: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117927

If the image has pulled successfully because either another pull secret did the job, or the image doesn't need auth, the warning is distracting.

As an example, this pod is running perfectly fine and has no problems, and yet when described, has had 11k warning events emitted over the last 9 days.
```
  Warning  FailedToRetrieveImagePullSecret  114s (x11399 over 9d)  kubelet  Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (sa-integration); attempting to pull the image may not succeed.
```

We have been including multiple pull secrets in our pulls because it's more flexible to point to a few that may exist than to have to very exactly map each pod to a pull secret. This change means we will get warnings even when everything is working exactly as we wanted it to.

### What did you expect to happen?

No warnings if an image is pulled successfully.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a pod or service account that references a missing pull secret that is not required to pull the image.

### Anything else we need to know?

My suggestion would be to only emit that warning if the image cannot be pulled (for example, reaches ImagePullBackOff), or to include the detail about the missing secret in the existing image pull failure events.

items.body:
### Which problem is this PR solving?

Fixes #141290

Pods using extended resource backed by DRA (KEP-5004, DRAExtendedResource) have their claim reference in `pod.Status.ExtendedResourceClaimStatus`, not in `pod.Spec.ResourceClaims`. The device-taint eviction controller only looked at `pod.Spec.ResourceClaims`, so NoExecute device taint eviction silently skipped pods that request devices via the extended resource field (e.g. `nvidia.com/gpu: 1`).

### Description of the changes

After the existing loop over `pod.Spec.ResourceClaims` in `podEvictionTime`, also check `pod.Status.ExtendedResourceClaimStatus` for the extended resource backed by DRA path. When present, look up the claim in `tc.allocatedClaims` and apply the same eviction logic.

This mirrors the same dual-location check already present in `pkg/controller/resourceclaim/controller.go`.

### How has this been tested?

Trivial change — the logic mirrors the existing pattern identically; no behavioral change for the `pod.Spec.ResourceClaims` path.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The reporter's issue body includes a complete live reproduction on a `kind` cluster (see #141290). I was unable to run the full integration test suite locally, but the change is a direct parallel of the existing pattern.

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #115823 - ContainerUnhealthy events from kubelet probes now indicate whether the failure was below the FailureThreshold (ignored) or reached it (action taken).

**Before**: Every probe failure emitted an identical `ContainerUnhealthy` event:
```
Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
```
Users had no way to distinguish between transient failures (below threshold) and failures that actually triggered a container restart.

**After**: Events now include threshold context:
```
Liveness probe failed (attempt 1/3, below threshold): HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
Liveness probe failed (threshold reached): HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
```

## Changes

- Moved event emission from `prober.probe()` to `worker.doProbe()` where the `resultRun` and `FailureThreshold` values are available
- Modified `prober.probe()` signature to also return the probe output string, so the worker can include diagnostic info in events
- Updated `prober_test.go` callers for the new signature

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #115823

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubelet: ContainerUnhealthy events from probes now indicate whether the failure was below the FailureThreshold (and therefore ignored) or exceeded it (action taken). For example: "Liveness probe failed (attempt 1/3, below threshold): ..." vs "Liveness probe failed (threshold reached): ..."
```

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `pkg/kubelet/prober` tests pass
- [x] `go build ./pkg/kubelet/prober/` succeeds

/sig node

items.body:
The scheduler knows which pods are on which nodes. It figures out all volumes on a node by the sum of its pods.  It does this to enforce constraints in a cloud environment.

It is possible to delete a PVC while a pod is still running.  The pod will continue to function, the PV remains attached to a node.  

When the scheduler attempts to place new pods on the node, it looks up all its existing PVs and their backing PVCs , except the PVC has been deleted, an error is thrown, and the scheduler fails.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/plugin/pkg/scheduler/algorithm/predicates/predicates.go#L157

The user gets an ugly error message about a namespace they don't own. Their pod won't run and the error message is confusing.

@kubernetes/rh-storage @kubernetes/sig-storage

items.body:
## what

I’m struggling to trigger image garbage collection (GC) by the kubelet process by simulating disk usage. In short, I can’t get it to work and can’t figure out if it’s a bug or a misunderstanding.  
## expectations
- Upon disk usage crossing the 90% threshold (default setting for `image-gc-high-threshold`) the kubelet will output messages to stdout or stderr indicating that it's vacuuming images
- A reduction of disk space below the high-watermark of 90%
## related

One of our problems was probably as a result of using a symlinked docker-root (see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/17994). We’ve since deployed the kubelet with `—docker-root=/vol/docker` as well as explicitly passed the `—graph=/vol/docker` directory to the docker daemon.  Despite these changes images are not being gc'd.
## reproduction

To simulate being out of space, I’ve created a `tmpfile` that uses up 89% of free space. 

```
dd if=/dev/zero of=/vol/docker/tmpfile bs=1G count=75
```

(I should have used a smaller volume!)

Disk space is now at 89% utilization as reported by `df`

Then I’ve downloaded 11G of docker images with `docker pull` by iterating over every release of an internal project to take me over the line to 91% as reported by `df`.

From what I observe from `journalctl` is that the `kubelet` is not performing any GC and the `df` does not change. I’ve also tried restarting the kublet to no avail.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

All code using the result of the generated client-go Informer() methods (a cache.SharedIndexInformer) constantly has to do type casts from "any" to the actual type of the objects managed by the informer.

This is:
- annoying at best
- often done inconsistently (should failed type assertions panic or be logged and if so, how?)
- a source of bugs (not handling DeletedFinalStateUnknown, type in event handler not matching the type in the informer)

In contrast, the Lister() result *is* typed. It converts without a type check in e.g. ResourceIndexer[T].List:

	err = cache.ListAllByNamespace(l.indexer, l.namespace, selector, func(m interface{}) {
		ret = append(ret, m.(T))
	})

This change here does the same wrapping for SharedIndexInformer, Indexer and index functions.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a Go API break because all generated interfaces change. See client-go CHANGELOG.md for details.

```release-note

```

items.body:
## What this does

Adds two new `kube-apiserver` flags:

| Flag | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--http2-write-byte-timeout` | `0` (disabled) | Close connections when no bytes can be written for this duration |
| `--http2-read-idle-timeout` | `0` (disabled) | Send a PING after this duration of no incoming frames; close on no PONG |

Also wires `http2.Server.CountError` to a new Prometheus counter `apiserver_http2_server_errors_total{type}` so ping timeouts and protocol violations are observable.

## Why

kube-apiserver has no connection-level write timeout. If an HTTP/2 client stops reading response bytes (receive buffer full), the server's `writeDataFromHandler` goroutine parks indefinitely in a select waiting for flow-control credit. The select has no `<-ctx.Done()` case, so the `WithTimeoutForNonLongRunningRequests` filter's 60s cancellation is never observed. The goroutine holds its APF seat until the underlying TCP connection dies.

This is the server-side behavior described in #111886. It is not client-specific — any HTTP/2 client whose response-body reader can stall will trigger it (slow consumer, killed process, blocked thread).

## Why not `http.Server.WriteTimeout`

That field sets a per-request total write deadline and would immediately kill all watch connections. `http2.Server.WriteByteTimeout` is different: the timer only runs **while a write is actively in progress** and resets whenever any bytes land on the wire. Idle watches — which have no pending writes — are completely unaffected.

## Why not KEP-4460 (per-request deadline via ResponseController)

That path was attempted in #114189 and hit a nil pointer panic in `net/http.(*http2pipe).CloseWithError`. The underlying Go issue (golang/go#65526, HTTP/1.x handler hang with SetWriteDeadline) has been open since 2024-02-05 with no movement. `WriteByteTimeout` operates at the connection layer below `ResponseController` and avoids both issues entirely.

## Behavior

- **Stalled LIST/GET** (client recv buffer full): server closes the connection after `--http2-write-byte-timeout`. Handler goroutine unblocks, APF seat released.
- **Healthy watch** (events flowing or quiet): write timeout never fires. Timer only runs during an active blocked write; no-write periods have no timer.
- **Dead peer** (`--http2-read-idle-timeout`): PING sent after idle interval; connection closed if no PONG within 15s.

Both flags default to `0` (disabled). No behavior change on existing clusters. Recommended value for `--http2-write-byte-timeout` when enabling: `60s`.

## Testing needed

- [ ] Unit test: stalled client connection closes within `WriteByteTimeout + ε`
- [ ] Unit test: active watch survives for `3× WriteByteTimeout` with no false close
- [ ] Unit test: `CountError` increments metric on ping timeout

Fixes #111886

items.body:
#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Adds Prometheus metrics for topology-aware scheduling (TAS) pod group placement, so the volume and latency of the placement evaluation phase can be observed.

3 alpha metrics are introduced, gated on the beta `TopologyAwareWorkloadScheduling` feature gate by default off (since they are only registered when TAS is enabled). Metrics are defined in [KEP-5732](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5732):

- `scheduler_generated_placements_total` counter of candidate placements generated when scheduling pod groups.
- `scheduler_placement_evaluations_total` counter of candidate placements evaluated when scheduling pod groups, split by `feasible`/`infeasible` result.
- `scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds` latency of evaluating a single candidate placement, split by `feasible`/`infeasible` result.

The TAS pod group placement algorithm phases:
1. generation: generate candidate placements 
2. evaluation: per placement loop try to fit each candidate
3. scoring: pick the best among feasible placements (only if there are more than 1 feasible placement)

The placement generation and scoring phases are intentionally not given dedicated metrics, since they are already covered by `scheduler_framework_extension_point_duration_seconds` with the [`PlacementGenerate`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L2076) and [`PlacementScore`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L1493) extension points. 
There is also existing `podgroup_scheduling_algorithm_duration_seconds` which measures the overall pod group scheduling cycle, so this PR focuses on the per-placement evaluation.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes [#139347](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/139347)

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Updated KEP metric names https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6234#event-27926380968

Output:
```
# HELP scheduler_generated_placements_total [ALPHA] Number of candidate placements generated when scheduling pod groups.
# TYPE scheduler_generated_placements_total counter
scheduler_generated_placements_total{profile="default-scheduler"} 5

# HELP scheduler_placement_evaluations_total [ALPHA] Number of candidate placements evaluated... 'feasible'... 'infeasible'...
# TYPE scheduler_placement_evaluations_total counter
scheduler_placement_evaluations_total{profile="default-scheduler",result="feasible"} 2
scheduler_placement_evaluations_total{profile="default-scheduler",result="infeasible"} 3

# HELP scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds [ALPHA] Latency in seconds...
# TYPE scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds histogram
scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds_bucket{...,result="feasible",le="0.001"} 1
...
scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds_sum{...,result="feasible"} 0.0127
scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds_count{...,result="feasible"} 2
```

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Scheduler metrics for the topology-aware scheduling (TAS) placement phases available when the TopologyAwareWorkloadScheduling feature gate is enabled: scheduler_generated_placements_total, scheduler_placement_evaluations_total, and scheduler_placement_evaluation_duration_seconds.
```

### What happened?

Executive Summary: `PATCH` endpoint doesn't honor or match `POST` endpoint `fieldValidation` and fails with 500 Internal Server Error instead of appropriately with 400 Bad Request or `Warning` header.

We're upgrading from K8S 1.20 to 1.28.(4) EKS and naturally encountering things that don't work.
Case in point here - Service topologyKeys that are gone.

items.body:
## What this PR does

This PR improves the error message when CEL selectors access non-existent device attributes. When users write expressions like `device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"` without checking if the attribute exists first, they currently get a generic "no such key" error with no guidance on how to fix it.

## Why this approach

### String matching for error detection

We detect "no such key" errors using `strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "no such key:")` instead of `errors.Is()` because:
- cel-go's `resolutionError` type is not exported (internal package)
- The cel-go library wraps errors in `types.Err` which only forwards the error message
- Kubernetes itself uses this pattern in apiextensions-apiserver (`staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/schema/cel/validation.go:759`)

### Why these three allocator files

The modification is applied to three allocator variants:
- `structured/internal/stable/allocator_stable.go`
- `structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go`
- `structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go`

These three files represent different maturity levels of the DRA allocator implementation. They must be kept in sync because:
1. They are the core CEL selector evaluation points in DRA
2. Features rotate between them as they mature (experimental → incubating → stable)
3. Maintaining consistency ensures behavior is preserved during rotation

### Error message references documentation

The enhanced error message links to `pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/resource/v1#CELDeviceSelector` instead of hardcoding examples. This ensures the error guidance stays current as the CEL documentation evolves with the codebase.

### Documentation improvements

We added concrete examples to `CELDeviceSelector` showing how to handle optional attributes using `orValue()`, `has()`, and the `?` operator. These examples demonstrate the robust patterns users should adopt to avoid "no such key" errors.

## Release note

```release-note
Improved CEL error messages in Dynamic Resource Allocation to provide guidance when accessing non-existent device attributes. Error messages now link to documentation on handling optional fields using orValue() and has().
```

## Related Issue

Fixes #135661

## Test

Added unit tests in `errors_test.go` to verify error enhancement behavior.

items.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR enhances the standard Pod-by-Pod preemption flow to support PodGroups as preemption victims. Previously, the preemption logic treated all pods individually. With this change, if a pod belongs to a PodGroup, the preemption logic can treat the group as a single atomic victim.

High-level overview of how this was achieved:
- **Interface Abstraction**: Introduced `Victim` and `DomainVictim` separation.
    - **`Victim`**: A general type used to generalize single Pods and `PodGroups`. It supports operations that do not depend on a specific preemption domain.
    - **`DomainVictim`**: Tied strictly to a preemption domain. It tracks `nodeInfos` (copies of node state, not active snapshot references, except WAP flow, for WAP we are using actual reference) representing the affected blast radius, which the preemption algorithm uses to identify pods for eviction. It cannot be created outside of a domain.
- **Constructor Methods**:
    - `NewVictim` signature was updated to return the `Victim` interface and made public.
    - Added `NewDomainForPodByPodPreemption` which initializes the preemption domain by grouping pods on a node by their `PodGroupName` (if applicable).
    - The `DomainVictim` constructor (`newDomainVictim`) calculates `nodeInfos` internally using a snapshot reference, rather than requiring them to be passed from outside the domain.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The changes focus on abstracting the "unit of preemption" into a `Victim` interface. The `NewDomainForPodByPodPreemption` constructor is where the grouping logic lives.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Enhanced Pod-by-Pod preemption to support PodGroups as preemption victims.
```
