#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Current http tunnel dial function could not be canceled when webhook request has been canceled. So, if the downtream is experiencing CPU saturation or networking issue, http tunnel will be stuck in dialing.

```plain
incoming API request
  -> kube-apiserver admission chain
    -> mutating/validating webhook HTTP client
      -> egress selector / HTTP CONNECT proxy
        -> konnectivity server/agent path
          -> webhook service/pod
```

For example, we have 1 second timeout for gatekeeper mutating webhook. But we got this log in kube-apiserver. Both the kube-apiserver and proxy server will maintain a lot of `established` connections until tunnel is ready.

```plain
Proxy via http_connect protocol over tcp" address:172.20.7.121:8443 20308ms...
```

To fix this, the egress selector applies a 30-second timeout when the
dial context has no deadline, matching http.DefaultTransport. For
webhook requests, net/http intentionally detaches dialing from the
request context, so the webhook timeout is not propagated to the dialer
and this default timeout normally applies. The proxy implementations
honor the dial deadline and clean up their underlying connections when
dialing fails or the returned connection is closed.

Manually benchmarking result:

* Env: 
   * Only one kube-apiserver + proxy + konnectivity-server.
      * They're running in the same node (v16cores)
      * There is stress process to consume 90% CPU resources
   * Gatekeeper webhook
      * One mutating webhook for all resources update and timeout in 1 second
      * One validating webhook for all resources update and timeout in 3 seconds
   * Only one konnectivity-agent and it's limited in 0.02 vcores (simulating slow tunnel)

* Traffic

There is an intentional breaking change to a Go type in this PR. Specifically, the Go type for the `MatchAttribute` and `DistinctAttribute` fields in `DeviceConstraint` has been changed from `FullyQualifiedName` to `QualifiedName`.  This change was made to accommodate attribute names without a domain prefix (for example, allowing `my-attribute` instead of requiring a domain like `example.com/my-attribute`) for derived attributes, which provides a better experience for users.

### What happened?

A node reboot event looks like this:
```
$ k get event kind-control-plane.186cd0d5e2253993 -oyaml
apiVersion: v1
count: 1
eventTime: null
firstTimestamp: "2025-10-09T11:59:31Z"
involvedObject:
  kind: Node
  name: kind-control-plane
  uid: kind-control-plane
kind: Event
lastTimestamp: "2025-10-09T11:59:31Z"
message: 'Node kind-control-plane has been rebooted, boot id: fda92249-bc38-49ea-b0c7-e664b214e43e'
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2025-10-09T11:59:34Z"
  name: kind-control-plane.186cd0d5e2253993
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "28264"
  uid: 7be02699-db88-4886-ae5c-f47be0b0c30c
reason: Rebooted
reportingComponent: kubelet
reportingInstance: kind-control-plane
source:
  component: kubelet
  host: kind-control-plane
type: Warning
```

This is missing `involvedObject.apiVersion`  and has the `uid` set to the name of the node rather than the uid.
This seems to be caused by using a `nodeRef` in the recorder as opposed to an actual node object: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3a53784ecbe4bed2aa0cbc159acbb56add05eef9/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L646

/sig node

### What did you expect to happen?

Correctly set involvedObject.apiVersion and uid fields

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Reboot a node

items.body: /kind bug #### What this PR does / why we need it: When a plugin is doing filter, each node will generate a event and send it to `r.bufferCh`. meanwhile, the buffer is flushed in every seconds. So if cluster is larger than the buffer size of channel, `r.bufferCh` can be easily full and overflowed. it cause plugin in later position barely have chance to be seen. This fix make sure the buffer can be flushed ASAP, to avoid channel overflow as much as possible. #### Which issue(s) this PR is related to: Fixes: #134972 #### Special notes for your reviewer: **Without** this fix, the chart in the bottom left, is evaluated by: ``` sum by (extension_point, status) (rate(scheduler_plugin_execution_duration_seconds_sum{plugin="DynamicResources"}[$__rate_interval])) ``` The line in the chart look very discontinuous, and in most time the duration of Filter only cost **0**. And with this fix, the chart looks normal now, and no performance regressed: Furthermore, the data in the chart appears similar to the previous E2E test with 100 nodes: https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests/pull/3368 https://prow.k8s.io/?job=ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-100-node-dra-with-workload #### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change? ```release-note none ``` #### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.: ```docs ```

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind documentation

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The purpose is two-fold:
- Raise awareness during PR review that a PR includes a breaking Go API change, as reported by apidiff ("incompatible change"). Previously, contributors and reviewers had to pay attention to the non-blocking apidiff jobs or catch changes manually.
- Document in client-go/CHANGELOG.md and apimachinery/CHANGELOG.md (disabled in a later commit, see individual commits for what it would look like) which breaking changes were made and how (if necessary) consumers of those packages can adapt to those changes. Previously they had to figure that out based on the source code diff and maybe some comments in the PR which made those changes.

As proof-of-concept, information about the changes in Kubernetes 1.35 and 1.36 are included. No attempt was made to explain the changes, they only include the title of the PR and a link to it. See commits for information how this was done automatically. We could go back further, if desired.

This is implemented in hack/apidiff.sh. Developers who are making a breaking change can use `hack/update-go-apidocs.sh` to add a new changelog entry. They still need to edit it before submitting the PR. The `hack/verify-go-apidocs.sh` checks that, but currently never fails (= not enforced yet, will be enabled in the future).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

@aojea, @skitt: this works pretty much as proposed at the meet&greet at KubeCon EU 2026.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138359 demonstrates how this would work in a PR which changes the client-go API.

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

kubectl uses k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml.YAMLReader to split streams into documents. That reader treats any line starting with --- as a document boundary.

With a file like:

```
%YAML 1.1
---
```

the splitter returns the first "document" as just %YAML 1.1\n (without the required document start marker), and the YAML→JSON conversion then fails with yaml: line 1: did not find expected <document start>.

The PR solves the issue such that when the reader sees a --- line and the buffer so far contains only directives (e.g. %YAML), treat that --- as the required document-start marker for the same document and include it in the buffer, instead of terminating the previous chunk.

items.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #124704 #121003

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The purpose of this PR is to resolve #124704

I have carefully introduced the causes of this problem and various solutions we've attempted to resolve it in https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TPrY56q9MNW8r1FuzKDFkBBhOjQ0hqi7wJAbIP1O-4g/

----
This PR proposes that during its execution cycle, `podWorkerLoop` should directly use the latest events reported by the container runtime as the current Pod state. If we can confirm that the events reported by the container runtime are reliable and up-to-date, we can stop relying on timestamps to determine whether the state is current. In both **Generic PLEG** and the current **Evented PLEG**, if the container state does not change, the timestamps in the cache are still updated unnecessarily (every 5 seconds and 1 second, respectively). This shows that timestamp-based checks are meaningless when the container state remains unchanged

The current container lifecycle code is not yet ready to directly receive status reported by the container runtime. To address this issue:

  1. The EventedPLEG needs to filter out sandbox creation and deletion events. This is because the container runtime reports events for sandbox containers and regular containers in the same way, which the kubelet has never handled before. Therefore, we have added an additional condition to ensure that creation events for sandbox containers do not trigger lifecycle processing before the creation of regular containers, and deletion events for sandbox containers do not trigger lifecycle processing after the deletion of regular containers.

  2. If syncPod needs to call the container runtime's API in any form to create/delete/update containers, we will actively list the container status after syncPod completes. This ensures the cache status remains synchronized with the latest container state and prevents subsequent EventedPLEG events from updating the cache and compromising its consistency.

NONE

items.title: Race in scheduler can cause infinite growth of inFlightEvents

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/scheduling
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Scheduling.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

items.body:
### What happened?

During the scheduling cycle if pod gets recreated with the same name during filtering there is a potential race condition causing the pod to stay in inFlightPods/inFlightEvents forever. 

Exact steps:

## Step 1: The Initial Lock-in
- Pop: The scheduler pops Pod-X (UID: AAAA) from the top of the scheduling queue.
- Record: The queue pushes Pod-X to the tail of the mixed doubly-linked `inFlightEvents` list to track when it started.
- Map: The queue stores the exact memory pointer to that list node inside `inFlightPods[AAAA]`.

## Step 2: The Synchronous Failure
- Execute: The scheduler begins running synchronous Filter plugins (e.g. checking NodeSelector, Taints, or custom filters).
- Fail: One of the filter plugins returns Unschedulable.
- Abort: Because scheduling cannot proceed, the scheduler aborts the cycle immediately and jumps straight to the failure handler. It skips `sched.SchedulingQueue.Done(assumedPod.UID)` done before bindingCycle.


## Step 3: The Recreation Overwrite (The Race Condition)
- Delete & Recreate: Just milliseconds before the failure handler runs, an external controller deletes Pod-X and immediately recreates a brand new instance with the exact same name/namespace, generating a new UID (BBBB).
- Fetch: The failure handler queries the local Informer cache for the latest state of the pod using its string name (Pod-X).
- Retrieve: The cache naturally returns the newly created instance with UID BBBB.
- Overwrite: The internal reference in the scheduler is updated to hold the new pod reference (BBBB).


## Step 4: Missing the Target
- Queue Push: The failure handler attempts to put the pod back into the queue using `AddUnschedulableIfNotPresent(BBBB)`.
- Deferred Done: The very first line of `AddUnschedulableIfNotPresent` function unconditionally executes:
``` go
       // In any case, this Pod will be moved back to the queue and we should call Done.
	defer p.Done(pInfo.Pod.UID)
```
- The Miss: `Done(BBBB)` looks inside the `inFlightPods` tracking map, sees that UID BBBB does not exist, and does absolutely nothing.
- The Ghost: The original UID (AAAA) is entirely forgotten by the system and remains permanently trapped inside the `inFlightPods` map and the doubly-linked list!

# Step 5: The Catastrophic Dam
- Drift: Over the next few seconds, as other unrelated pods complete their cycles normally, they get removed from the front of the list. The trapped ghost pod (AAAA) eventually shifts all the way to the Front() position of the list.
- The Blockade: Because `Done(AAAA)` is never called, this node can never be removed from Front().
- Paralysis: Every time the cleanup routine attempts to run, it looks at the very first element of the list, sees the ghost pod (AAAA), and completely halts all pruning to protect it.
- The Explosion: Meanwhile, standard background updates (Node usage, endpoint slices, system leases) continuously append thousands of new *clusterEvent nodes to the tail of the linked list. Because the front node is anchored forever, none of those incoming events can ever be deleted—causing your InFlightEvents metric to grow infinitely 

### What did you expect to happen?

The Done method of scheduling queue should be called on the old UID. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Integration test `TestInFlightPodLeak` added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...Argh4k:kubernetes:potential-memory-leak reproduces that locally. 

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

Observed on a cluster running v1.34.1, but still reproducible with the HEAD.

### Cloud provider

Observed on a cluster running on GKE but reproducible on a HEAD.


### OS version

N/A

### Install tools

N/A

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

N/A

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

N/A

labels.name: needs-sig

items.body:
### What happened?

On EKS clusters running kubelet `v1.34.4-eks-f69f56f` on Bottlerocket 1.57.0 (`aws-k8s-1.34`), a subset of nodes appear to silently skip serving-certificate rotation entirely.

The initial bootstrap CSR is issued at node boot and approved normally by EKS's built-in CSR approver. After that, for the full life of the affected node (38+ days observed):

- `kubelet_certificate_manager_server_rotation_seconds_count` stays at `0`.
- `kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors == 0`.
- No CSR is ever submitted from the node (`kubectl get csr` shows none from the affected node while sibling nodes' CSRs exist and are approved).
- `journalctl -u kubelet --since -40d | grep -iE "certificate_manager|csr|rotat|serving cert"` returns only the initial-bootstrap `"no serving certificate available for the kubelet"` TLS handshake errors from the first minute of boot. Nothing afterward.
- The serving cert's `NotAfter` passes through the usual rotation threshold (~day 30 of its ~45-day lifetime) without any attempt, and eventually triggers the `KubeletServerCertificateExpiration` alert.

Only one cert file exists on disk:

```
-rw-------.  1 root root 1256 Mar 27 15:34 kubelet-server-2026-03-27-15-34-40.pem
lrwxrwxrwx.  1 root root   59 Mar 27 15:34 kubelet-server-current.pem -> .../kubelet-server-2026-03-27-15-34-40.pem
```

Kubelet PID is unchanged for the full 38 days (process never restarted/crashed). Node is `Ready`, heartbeats OK, `node.status.addresses` populated on the API server.

I'm not 100% sure this is a kubelet bug rather than something I've missed in our setup — posting cautiously in case someone more familiar with the cert-manager code can sanity-check. I believe I've ruled out the usual config/infra suspects (see "Anything else" below).

**Related, already-closed issues/PRs I reviewed:**

- #130001 (Kubelet serving CSR never created)
- #130415 (node reports Ready before server CSR created → templates never populate)
- #130409 (link-local IPv6 → no addresses → no CSR)
- Fix PR #130362 "Use node addresses from informer in kubelet certificate manager" (merged 2025-04-25, confirmed present in v1.34.4 via `git log --contains`)

The symptom here is in the same family as #130415 but on the *rotation* path rather than initial bootstrap (the initial bootstrap CSR *does* succeed). So I suspect the 2025-04 fix may not fully cover the rotation-deadline path.

**Speculative root-cause trace (please sanity-check):**

Tracing v1.34.4:

- `pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:900` constructs the server cert manager with `klet.getLastObservedNodeAddresses` as the `getAddresses` callback.
- `pkg/kubelet/kubelet_getters.go:472` implements it as `kl.GetNode()` → `kl.nodeLister.Get(nodeName)` on a per-node field-selector-filtered SharedInformer (`pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:465-475`).
- `pkg/kubelet/certificate/kubelet.go:47` `newGetTemplateFn` returns `nil` when `len(ips) == 0`.
- `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go:449-452`:

  ```go
  // Don't enter rotateCerts and trigger backoff if we don't even have a template to request yet
  if m.getTemplate() == nil {
      return
  }
  ```

If at the moment the rotation deadline fires the per-node informer transiently returns an empty `status.addresses` (or the goroutine evaluating `getTemplate()` races with informer re-list/resync), the rotation function `return`s **without rescheduling**. The only way it re-enters is via a template-changed watch event — so if no subsequent event makes the template transition (informer already settled at the same state), the rotation loop never re-fires for the lifetime of the kubelet.

That code shape — a silent early return with no retry timer — would explain the exact pattern we see (zero attempts, zero errors, zero logs, across 38 days of uptime). PR #130362 moved the *initial* template sourcing off a field that depended on the node-status-update loop, but the rotation-deadline path still depends on `nodeLister.Get()` returning a populated `status.addresses`.

I may be wrong about the root cause — if someone who knows this code can confirm/deny the race, I'd be happy to add `klog.V(2)` around the `return` at `:449` to distinguish "template nil" from "template matches last" on long-running nodes.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:

- The cert-manager wakes at `nextRotationDeadline` (~day 30 of a 45-day cert), submits a CSR, and logs `"Certificate rotation deadline determined"` / `"Certificate template changed, rotating"` from `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go`;

- OR a failure increments `kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors` with a descriptive log line.

On the affected nodes, neither happens — the rotation loop appears to either never start or to exit early before reaching `rotateCerts`, and stays silent for the rest of the node's life.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I don't have a deterministic reproducer — it looks probabilistic at boot.

Environment where it reliably reproduces at roughly 15–20% per-node rate:

1. EKS 1.34 control plane (tested with `v1.34.6-eks-bbe087e`).
2. Bottlerocket `aws-k8s-1.34` v1.57.0 nodes, kubelet `v1.34.4-eks-f69f56f`.
3. Kubelet config: `serverTLSBootstrap: true`, default `RotateKubeletServerCertificate` (enabled), no flag overrides.
4. EKS built-in kube-controller-manager CSR auto-approver (no external approver needed — sibling nodes' CSRs approve with message `"Auto approving self kubelet server certificate after SubjectAccessReview"` which matches upstream `pkg/controller/certificates/approver/sarapprove.go`).
5. Karpenter-managed on-demand nodes.

Observation procedure on any long-lived node:

```
# On apiserver
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/metrics" \
  | grep -E 'kubelet_certificate_manager_server_(ttl_seconds|rotation_seconds_count)|kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors'

# On node (via Bottlerocket admin container):
sheltie ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/pki/
sheltie journalctl -u kubelet --since $(boot-time) | grep -iE "certificate_manager|csr|rotat|serving cert"
```

Across a prod cluster of ~115 non-Fargate nodes, 6 system-nodes booted within the same minute from the same AMI / same NodePool / same IAM role / same kubelet config:

- 5 rotated cleanly at ~day 35 (`rotation_seconds_count == 1`, matching CSR present and approved).
- 1 did not (`rotation_seconds_count == 0` at day 38, no CSR ever requested).

Fleet-wide across four EKS 1.34 clusters: ~15–20% of nodes that survive past the rotation window silently fail to rotate. Most of our churn replaces nodes before the rotation window fires, which is why the bug is easy to miss on faster-churning clusters.

Happy to capture additional diagnostics on a confirmed-affected node if it would help — goroutine dump, `klog -v=4` after kubelet restart (though restart may mask the bug), captured CSR history from siblings, etc.

### Anything else we need to know?

**Config I was able to rule out before posting:**

- `serverTLSBootstrap: true` in kubelet config (Bottlerocket ships this default in `sources/shared-defaults/kubernetes-aws.toml`), confirmed via `apiclient get settings.kubernetes.server-tls-bootstrap`.
- `RotateKubeletServerCertificate` feature gate — GA since 1.12, enabled by default, no flag overrides on our end.
- `rotateCertificates` — default `true` in `KubeletConfiguration`.
- EKS CSR auto-approver is working (same cluster, same approver, approves 5/6 sibling CSRs cleanly).
- RBAC / IAM — identical to siblings that rotate fine.
- Node clock — node posts heartbeats correctly.

Six sibling nodes booted **within the same minute** from the same Karpenter NodeClass (identical AMI, kubelet flags, NodePool, IAM role, subnet, VPC). Five rotated; one didn't. That isolates the fault to kubelet-internal rotation logic, not our config / approver / infra.

**Fleet-wide impact** (for sense of scope, not for dramatic effect):

- Prod `application` cluster: 101/115 non-Fargate nodes currently have `rotation_seconds_count=0`. Most are too young to have entered the rotation window — the bug is latent, only materializing on nodes that survive past ~day 30–35.
- Our workaround: reducing Karpenter `expireAfter` from 100d to 35d to guarantee nodes are replaced before the rotation window is ever reached. This avoids the alert but doesn't surface the underlying bug.

**Why I chose "probably a bug" rather than user error:** given identical config across 6 nodes with 5 rotating cleanly, I don't see a config-level explanation. Happy to be told otherwise.

### Kubernetes version

items.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Makes Topology-Aware Workload Scheduling (TAS) respect `NominatedNodeName` (NNN) when picking a placement for a PodGroup. Today TAS ranks placements by score and a random tiebreak, ignoring NNN, so a gang nominated to specific nodes can land elsewhere. Pod-by-pod scheduling already tries the nominated node first; this closes the gap at the placement level.

The core scheduler now evaluates the placement matching the pods' NNN before any other. If the gang is feasible there, it uses that placement and skips the rest. Otherwise it falls back to the normal score-based selection across all placements.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #139348
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5732

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Nominated placement first: mirrors pod-by-pod scheduling, which tries the nominated node before all others. A nominated node is usually set by a prior preemption cycle, so it's the placement the gang is expected to land on.
- Short-circuit only when the gang is feasible on the nominated placement now, not via preemption. If it isn't, the nominated placement competes with the rest under normal scoring, so NNN never schedules fewer pods.
- When nominations span more than one placement, no single placement clearly matches, so we skip the shortcut and fall back to normal scoring. This keeps the result independent of the order plugins hand us placements.
- Test plumbing: steps framework gained `UpdatePodStatus` and a `WaitForPodsNominated` barrier so the integration test sets NNN before the gang's cycle without racing.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-scheduler: TAS placement selection now respects NominatedNodeName. This does not yet apply to PodGroups belonging to a CompositePodGroup; see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140863.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5732
```
